subject: 🏃 Saturday — Full Rest (Wk 7, Presidio HM Eve)
html:
Tomorrow: full rest. No run, no gym, no shakeout. The only job is to arrive at Sunday's start line fresh, fueled, and calm. The taper is done — Tuesday's threshold was dead-even at 7:09–7:13/mi, Thursday's progression was well-governed, Friday's strides were clean with the knee at 1/5. You're sharp.

Saturday checklist:

  • Lay out race kit — shoes, H10 strap (charge it tonight), watch, bib, hat/visor, whatever you're carrying water in. Decide now, not at 5 AM.
  • Pre-check PF30 gels — pull-test the tear notch on 3–4 pouches one-handed, dry run. Set aside any that don't pop clean. You'll want at least 3 for a ~97-min HM (1 at T−5, then every 30 min).
  • Hydration — drink steadily all day, aim for pale-straw urine by bedtime. Half an LMNT packet in water with dinner is a good pre-load.
  • Dinner — familiar, carb-forward, moderate volume. Pasta, rice bowl, or oatmeal — nothing new, nothing heavy. Keep protein moderate, fat low. Learn from the PAL 10K: the heavier-than-usual breakfast drove a stitch. Light and boring wins.

Focus cue for the weekend: Mentally walk through the race plan tonight or tomorrow. Internalize the mile-by-mile pacing from RACE_PLAN_PRESIDIO.md — especially mile 1 (7:25, resist the adrenaline), the climb miles (7:35–7:40, effort-governed), and the mile 10 decision point. The three gates are sub-1:37:30 / HR <170 final 3 mi / zero knee comp. You know this; let it settle in so Sunday morning is automatic.

Where you are: Week 7 of 12, Phase 2. This is the pivot test — the one race in the plan that determines whether the SF Marathon target stays 3:30 or upgrades to 3:25. The data says you're ready: knee 1/5 across the entire taper, threshold pace sitting 7:09–7:13 at HR 155–158, the June 14 14-miler absorbed clean with a 5-mi MP finish. Trust the preparation.

Bed by 10 tonight. Tomorrow night's briefing will have the full race-morning fueling plan and final logistics. Sleep well.
